text: Create Journal in Spreadsheet is one of the most commonly used ADFdi actions in General Ledger, and it's a useful first example because you already know the business rule it enforces — the same balancing rule from lesson fifteen, through a completely different mechanical path.

From General Accounting, in the Journals work area, Create Journal in Spreadsheet launches a connected Excel workbook, provided the ADFdi add-in is already installed. It isn't a blank template — it's pre-connected to your ledger and chart of accounts through the ADFdi ribbon.

A user enters journal lines directly: account combination, debit or credit, currency, description. No CSV generation, no ZIP, no UCM upload. The ADFdi ribbon has its own upload action that submits the rows directly. The entire chapter-one pipeline collapses into one click inside the spreadsheet.

Because ADFdi talks to the live application directly, a lot of validation happens close to the moment of upload. An invalid account combination, or a batch that doesn't balance, can be flagged back within the same session — a much faster feedback loop than waiting on a scheduled process report.

Ten journal lines posting this afternoon are a poor fit for the FBDI pipeline — too much ceremony for ten rows. Create Journal in Spreadsheet is built for exactly this scale. Nobody's typing ten thousand lines into a spreadsheet by hand, which is exactly why FBDI exists for that end of the scale. Up next, lesson twenty-six: uploading Payables invoices with ADFdi.
